newsitem.title: NIGER: Strike cuts power in Niger.
newsitem.headline: Strike cuts power in Niger.

text.p: A wildcat strike by power workers in the West African state of Niger halted supplies to the capital Niamey on Friday and plunged it into darkness, witnesses and union sources said.
The national power workers union SYNATREN called an indefinite strike by the 1,000 workers at the Niger Electricity Company NIGELEC to demand the release of about 10 union militants.

The union opposes plans to include NIGELEC among about a dozen companies to be privatised. Police sources say the militants were arrested after sabotage during earlier strikes to parts of the electricity network.
The union called a strike on February 18 and 19 to protest against privatisation.
Its members stopped work on March 5 and 6 and March 18 and 19 following calls from Niger's main umbrella union grouping the USTN for a broader civil service strike.
Medical sources said a prolonged strike could pose serious problems at the capital's two main hospitals where obsolete generators are unable to keep all the services running.
